$comment: SHARED CONTRACT -- the EXPRESSION seam: what does this expression answer over these rows?
One grammar, two calculators (lead 0b7d84462): the server's (chain decide aggregations, walk measures) and the
screen's (the test bed's calculated values). Both read THIS file: server/expression.py and client2/src/expression.js.
THE GRAMMAR is Spotfire's expression language (task/SPOTFIRE_FUNCTIONS.md, read from the owner's Spotfire
Analyst 14.4.1) plus our [path] · type("key") · Reach (afcb79f14). Only Spotfire's part is here; [x] is a
column of `rows`.
EVERY EXPECTATION IS A DOCUMENT'S, NOT A MEASUREMENT (lead 10-13). The owner's Spotfire web view opens its
expression windows on the owner's desktop, so the empty-value cases the dialog text leaves open were not
measured. `basis` says how each answer was reached:
doc-stated  the cited page prints this result for this expression
doc-rule    the cited page states the rule; the answer applies it (computed, not typed)
measured    run in Spotfire - none in this edition
graph         a vector that carries `graph` (a walk answer's nodes and edges) names its `rows` by node id; [a.b~.x] walks
that graph from the row (a way: steps joined by «.», «~» backwards, the value's name last).
screen_only   Marked() reads the page's markings - `markings` fakes the page: {name: {in: [ids], unknown: [ids]}}, every other
node out. The server's calculator has no markings and refuses the name.
`cells` {A1: value} fakes a sheet's cells (owner 3b97fcfb9: cell references A1 and ranges B1:B9 are the
sheet's grammar); `nodes` {type: [its keys in declared order]} the page's node types for type("key", ...),
whose answer is the node's id (rnd_board/api.js entitySeedId). The server refuses both by name.
ours        our rule (the cite names the ruling) - only in `ours`
decided     no page settles it; the lead ruled it 10-13 from the nearest rule the cite names. «may differ from
Spotfire» in a cite marks a ruling Spotfire may answer otherwise, with no way left to measure it
Pages (`sources`): Spotfire's «latest» online reference, read 2026-10-13 (Math Stat Ops Prec Logic Keys Lang Text), and the
7.0.1 statistics definitions (701), against the owner's 14.4.1. An invalid value (#NA, an error) is read as empty, as the
pages print 0/0 and Integer("0%") - that reading is itself a doc-rule. A comparison the page prints only through
If(<it>, "true", "false") or a Case is scored bare: If gives true, false and null back one to one (Logic If).
HOW TO SCORE
vectors       scored. `expect` = the one answer over `rows` (an aggregation folds them; a constant needs none;
a one-argument aggregate is a fold over `rows`, so it always carries at least one row);
`expect_rows` = one answer per row, in row order. A vector carries exactly one of the two.
null = empty. Numbers equal when |got - expect| <= 1e-9 * max(1, |expect|). Integer / Real /
Decimal types are not scored.
`types` {column: "datetime"} (table_config's column_types words): Min and Max over a datetime
column compare instants and answer the row's value as written (lead 10-13, basis decided).
unsettled     NOT scored - where an open cell goes: what is open and why. To settle one, move it into vectors
with its basis; do not pick an answer in a calculator. Empty after the lead's 10-13 rulings.
An aggregate inside an If / Case branch folds only that branch's rows (the pages' worked examples).
ours          scored, the same shape - our functions with no Spotfire basis (task doc §7: Latest). A row's
values carry that row's time in "$at" (ISO 8601); [x] never names it. basis = ours, or decided.
Rules both calculators keep (lead 10-13): Latest - with any timed row, the latest of the timed rows
(an untimed row is not a candidate); with none timed, the value when there is one or all agree, else
empty; two different values at the latest time are empty. A list value (one read holding several)
counts as its items. A text is a number when, trimmed, it is only sign, digits, a decimal point and
which a numeric fold leaves out; an empty text is empty.
out_of_edition  names not built in this edition, and why.
The functions themselves - names, args, counts, the names refused and every refusal sentence - are
contracts/expression/catalogue.json, written from the server's table (owner 11-09 «ㄴ»).
Grow this file before a calculator grows (lead: a function with no vector is not built).
DATES (lead fe2ba4b1f): a vector with `zone` (an IANA name) is answered with the dates cut on that zone's wall clock -
the product reads it from ingestion_settings "expression_time_zone", Asia/Seoul (owner «ㅇㅇ kst»). A time with an
offset is moved into the zone; one without is that zone's wall clock. Date and DateTime answer a time text
(«2026-10-14T00:00:00+09:00», «Z» at offset 0). `expect_not_time`: the rows a date function met a value that is not
a time on (an empty value is not counted).
TEXTS IN QUOTES (lead 11-09 ①): \\ \" \' inside quotes are that character; any other \x is itself. PATTERNS
(RXExtract · RXReplace · ~=): only what Python's re, JavaScript's RegExp and .NET read alike - task doc «Patterns».
PARSEDATETIME (owner 11-07 «2»): ParseDateTime(text, format), the format in Spotfire's .NET spelling - a closed set:
yyyy yy MM dd HH mm ss fff, quoted text ('...' or "..."), a backslash-escaped letter, any other character as itself.
The text matches it exactly - the digits each token names, nothing more, no other separator. yy is .NET's window
(TwoDigitYearMax 2029): 00-29 is 20xx, 30-99 is 19xx. The year, month and day are named. Read on the zone's wall clock
and answered as DateTime spells a time; a text that is not that shape or not a real time is empty and counted
(`expect_not_time`). A format outside the set, or not a text in quotes, is refused when the expression is read:
`expect_refused` is the sentence compile answers with (`rows` then empty).
